eligibility.quote: Generates the points and sends them to executor, but that throws an error.
eligibility.reason: The reproduced Panda case sends a planner-produced trajectory to a separate controller, which rejects its time values. Both concrete reproducer and log are present. This is a PAIR interface-value failure, not an internal-only planner defect, even though the resolving edit is in the planner.

failed_conditions.quote: Using `pilz_industrial_motion_planner` to generate a motionsequence with a blend radius generates (multiple) points with the same value for `RobotTrajectory.joint_trajectory.points[].time_from_start`.
failed_conditions.reason: Strictly increasing trajectory time is a value constraint, fitting other. The log identifies panda_arm_controller, and its pinned source constructs the follow_joint_trajectory endpoint from that node name, supporting the listed action as well as time_from_start.

loudness.quote: [ros2_control_node-5] [ERROR] [1710412387.951283595] [panda_arm_controller]: Time between points 122 and 123 is not strictly increasing, it is 12.200000 and 12.200000 respectively
loudness.reason: The controller explicitly validates and refuses the goal. S1's opening instruction specifically says to include runtime-enforced refusals and mark them loud_documented; that instruction supports loud here even though the stage is run.

detection_stage.reason: Detection happens when an already running controller receives and validates the action goal, not during node/controller activation or initial connection.

resolution.quote: I was unable to test moveit/moveit2_tutorials#917 successfully on Rolling/main because there was an issue with sending duplicate time points to joint trajectory controllers with the Pilz move group sequence capability.
resolution.reason: The fix author reports success for a Rolling tutorial and confirms the subsequent root-cause fix in PR 2961, but this does not identify both units of the reporter's Iron/Panda resolved pair. recommended is appropriate for the specified revisions.

notes: Read issue 2741 including runtime log and workaround discussion, PRs 2943/2961 and the latter diff, and pinned controller validation/action-server code. Jitter introduced by timing workarounds belongs to changed compositions, not an additional failed condition of the original rejection. The Pilz unit label abbreviates the MoveIt-side planner/action-client pipeline rather than claiming the planner plugin directly creates the action client.
